The National Agricultural Development Fund has distributed agricultural inputs to 8,000 rice and maize farmers in Ogun State whose crops were destroyed by flooding during the 2026 rainy season. The intervention, flagged off in Abeokuta, the state capital, on Monday in collaboration with the state government, is part of the NADF’s emergency agricultural recovery programme aimed at helping affected farmers resume production and recover their livelihoods. The beneficiaries comprise 4,000 rice farmers and 4,000 maize farmers, who are expected to receive improved seeds, fertilisers, herbicides, pesticides and other farm inputs. Speaking at the event, the Executive Secretary and Chief Executive Officer of NADF, Mohammed Ibrahim, represented by Olakunle Dabiri, said the programme was designed to prevent farmers from losing an entire planting season because of the floods. He said the intervention was being implemented in six states across the South-South, South-West and North-Central regions, with rice farmers in Bayelsa, Akwa Ibom, Benue and Kogi also expected to benefit. He said the programme would be implemented within seven weeks, with beneficiaries verified to ensure transparency in the distribution of the inputs. The NADF chief added that the intervention would also promote climate-smart agricultural practices, early-warning systems and agricultural insurance to reduce farmers’ vulnerability to future disasters. Owotomo recalled that the NADF had supplied more than 20,000 bags of fertiliser to farmers in the state during the planting season earlier in the year. He appealed to the fund to extend its support to cotton farmers in Ogun, saying the state was seeking to increase production ahead of the commencement of operations at a proposed cotton processing facility in its industrial zone. “Ogun actually produces the best cotton as far as Nigeria is concerned. We will be looking for support in that regard,” he said. He added that cotton farmers needed assistance to boost production before the facility commenced operations, urging the NADF to partner with the state government in supporting them. Taiwo Bankole
